audience.text: Go developers building server-side or cross-platform applications that require PDF processing without native dependencies.

capabilities.text: Split, merge, extract, rotate, reorder, and insert pages; manage page labels, Info and XMP metadata, and page geometry boxes.
capabilities.title: Page operations and metadata

capabilities.text: Password-protect documents with AES-128/256 or RC4, set granular permissions, sign with PKCS#7/PAdES/timestamps, verify signatures, and support certificate-based encryption.
capabilities.title: Encryption and digital signatures

capabilities.text: Lay out paragraphs, headings, images, tables, and lists top-to-bottom with automatic pagination, floating boxes, and multi-column support.
capabilities.title: Content authoring with Flow layout

capabilities.text: Build multi-page tables with repeating headers, cell merging, and styling; draw lines, rectangles, circles, paths, gradients, and tiling patterns.
capabilities.title: Tables and vector graphics

capabilities.text: Create and edit text, checkbox, radio, combo, list, push button, password, file select, rich text, number, date, and barcode fields; manage annotations and stamps.
capabilities.title: AcroForms and annotations

capabilities.text: Validate structural integrity, PDF/A-1/2/3 conformance, and PDF/UA-1 accessibility; convert documents toward conformance; build Tagged PDF structure trees.
capabilities.title: PDF/A and accessibility validation

capabilities.text: Render pages to PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP, and TIFF; convert to/from HTML, SVG, Markdown, DOCX, XLSX, and EPUB; extract text and images with layout.
capabilities.title: Rendering and format conversion

capabilities.text: Compare documents page-by-page or flat, generate markup highlights, use AI copilots for summarization, OCR, chat, and alt-text generation over OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
capabilities.title: Document comparison and AI copilots

limitations.text: Linearization cannot be combined with encryption or digital signing in the same document.
Certificate-based encryption accepts RSA recipients only; elliptic curve recipients and legacy RC4 sub-filters are not written.
OpenType shaping covers Arabic-family, Hebrew, and simple scripts; Indic, Khmer, Myanmar, and Hangul reordering shapers and vertical text are not implemented.
ConvertToPDFA does not flatten transparency; call FlattenTransparency separately before converting to PDF/A-1.
SearchText and ReplaceText match within a single text line only; queries that straddle line breaks are not found.
The built-in renderer does not support mesh shadings (PDF shading types 4-7).

problems_solved.text: Enables PDF creation, editing, and conversion in pure Go without CGo, native libraries, or third-party dependencies.
Provides document comparison, OCR, and AI copilots for summarization, chat, and alt-text generation over OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
Supports PDF/A and PDF/UA validation and conversion, digital signatures (PKCS#7, PAdES, timestamps), and encryption (AES-128/256, certificate-based).
Offers layout engines (Flow), table detection, and conversion to HTML, SVG, Markdown, DOCX, XLSX, and EPUB.

product_summary.text: Aspose.PDF FOSS for Go is a pure Go library for creating, editing, converting, and validating PDF documents without CGo or external dependencies.

uncertainties: The exact set of supported PDF/A-1/2/3 subtypes and validation rules for PDF/UA-1 is not fully detailed beyond basic conformance checks.
Whether the AI copilots support non-English languages beyond the OcrOptions.Font and SummaryOptions.Language settings is unclear.
The behavior of Table when RowSpan groups split across page breaks is not specified.
Whether content-driven auto-fit column widths are supported in Table is not confirmed.
The exact set of unsupported SVG features beyond textPath, vertical writing, external images, Gaussian blur, and em/ex/% units is not listed.
Whether the renderer handles isolated/knockout transparency groups is not confirmed.
The exact behavior of ConvertToPDFA for fonts with embedding restrictions is not detailed.
Whether the TableAbsorber detects borderless tables in complex layouts is not specified.

workflows.name: Split and merge PDFs
workflows.text: Open a PDF with pdf.Open, call doc.Split() to create per-page documents, or use doc.Append(b) to merge documents in place, then save results.

workflows.name: Create documents with Flow layout
workflows.text: Call pdf.NewDocumentFromFormat, create a flow with doc.NewFlow, add headings, paragraphs, lists, and tables, then call flow.Render() to paginate.

workflows.name: Encrypt and sign documents
workflows.text: Set encryption with doc.SetEncryption, write to a buffer, and verify opening returns ErrEncrypted; sign with doc.Sign using a crypto.Signer and certificate.

workflows.name: Render pages to images
workflows.text: Call doc.RenderImage(pageIndex, opts) to render a page to an image, or use page.RenderPNG/RenderJPEG/etc. for direct format output.

workflows.name: Build and render tables
workflows.text: Create a table with pdf.NewTable, set column widths, borders, margins, and cell styles, add rows and cells, then add it to a page with page.AddTable.

workflows.name: Use AI copilots
workflows.text: Initialize ai.NewSummaryCopilot, ai.NewChatCopilot, ai.NewOcrCopilot, or ai.NewImageDescriptionCopilot, configure options, and call their methods over an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
